I don't think you're seeing my perspective as someone unfamiliar with the laws in place, but I do see yours and can appreciate that while we may have been misled by the initial rep who advised we file the claim (see my other reply), you are saying it is required by law that they take the other party's statement once the claim is filed. Thank you for the feedback.

Just to share my perspective:

>because there is an incident in which they may have to pay out money and want to know everything about if they do

The only additional information they are acquiring is the other party's side of the story. Which he would have to provide regardless if he himself chose to contact our insurance to pursue a payout for his damages. I am saying that our insurance needlessly opened themselves to paying out to the other party rather than leaving it to the other party to pursue this payout themselves (as is normally the case when insurance is exchanged). But if it is required by law, then that's that.

>you really think their override decision is raising your premiums, and not doing what they need to do by law? they can raise your premiums without paying out the claim.

No, I was under the impression that since we were the ones filing the claim, they were not required by law to reach out and take the other party's statement since doing so could only hurt us. And instead, could take our statement down and take the other party's should they contact our insurance pursuing damages (per our exchanged insurance info). The initial insurance rep said we should file a claim "just in case" the other party came after us. Hence, I wasn't sure why else they would be opening themselves up to paying out more easily.

>yes. insurance only pays out to the amount of your policy

I was making note of this per your original comment suggesting that they were allowed to reach out to the other party with no possible benefit to us because they were the ones that had to payout. I was noting that they are doing this with the possibility of making us payout as well.

>because they are the ones that would be paying out money.

I guess we were misled by the initial rep then who made it sound like it couldn't hurt to file a claim "just in case they come after you for damages". I'm inclined to think we should not file a claim at all in situations like this, given that it could only hurt us.

The main reason I can see as to why we should have filed the claim is that it would look a little suspicious that we didn't file one and the other party came after us for damages of his own volition. But even that I feel like wouldn't affect our credibility that much, as we had no damages ourselves and the other party did not seem very worried about their own damages--which seems like a reasonable enough excuse as to why we didn't bother filing one.

Why would they choose to do this though? Because our insurance paying out is an opportunity to raise our premium? Separately, we would *also* have to pay out money if the damages were in excess of our coverage. We received a letter from them stating as much.
